skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Backend development guidelines for Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Sentry, Zod validation, configuration, middleware, testing, and layered service design.
skill.summary: Guide Node.js teams through consistent Express, TypeScript, Prisma, validation, monitoring, and testing patterns.
skill.author: diet103

security_audit.summary: Static analysis findings are mostly false positives from markdown examples, relative imports, configuration snippets, and backend documentation. No prompt injection or malicious execution intent was found, but the skill includes risky guidance around broad Sentry telemetry and copyable secret examples.

remediation.suggestion: Disable local variable capture and request body capture by default. Include only fields required for debugging and document privacy review steps.

remediation.issue: Copyable secret placeholders and config precedence
remediation.suggestion: Replace weak sample secrets with generated placeholders and make production examples reject defaults, empty secrets, and committed config files.

remediation.issue: Security scanners flag many markdown examples
remediation.suggestion: Label risky snippets as examples, explain safe boundaries, and avoid production-looking secret values in documentation.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Sentry Telemetry May Expose PII
semantic_findings.description: The Sentry template enables local variables and request data, including bodies, headers, IP addresses, query strings, URLs, and user identifiers. This can send sensitive application data to an external service unless each field is minimized.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented Sentry configuration explicitly includes request data, headers, IP addresses, query strings, URLs, user identifiers, and local variables. The later header scrub does not remove body data, IP addresses, query strings, usernames, or local variable values.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Secret Configuration Examples
semantic_findings.description: The configuration guide shows weak placeholder secrets, database passwords, token values, and config.ini precedence above environment variables. Users could copy these patterns into production without stronger secret generation and validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited section contains sample database passwords, token secrets, Keycloak secrets, and an environment override with DB_PASSWORD. The file later warns not to commit secrets, so this is guidance risk rather than clear malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Backend teams often struggle with inconsistent routes, services, validation, and monitoring. This skill provides practical patterns for structured Node.js services.
actual_capabilities: Explains layered route, controller, service, and repository architecture.
Provides Express controller and middleware patterns with error handling.
Shows Prisma repository, transaction, and database access guidance.
Documents Zod validation patterns for requests, DTOs, and errors.
Covers Sentry setup, performance monitoring, and async error handling.
Includes testing guidance for unit, integration, and authenticated routes.
limitations: The skill is documentation only and does not run code by itself.
Examples are tailored to Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, and Sentry.
Security-sensitive examples require review before production use.
It does not replace project-specific architecture or compliance requirements.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Structure
use_cases.description: Use the architecture guide to align routes, controllers, services, repositories, validation, monitoring, and tests.

use_cases.title: Implement New API Features
use_cases.description: Follow the examples to create endpoints with validation, error handling, service logic, and Prisma access.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Routes
use_cases.description: Move business logic out of route files and into controllers, services, repositories, and reusable middleware.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Route
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new endpoint pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-dev-guidelines to design a simple Express route and controller for a new user profile endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation And Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-dev-guidelines to add Zod validation and consistent error handling to this Express controller.

prompt_templates.title: Design Service And Repository Layers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for layered business logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-dev-guidelines to split this feature into controller, service, repository, and test responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Production Backend Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across architecture, security, and operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-dev-guidelines to review this backend change for architecture, validation, Sentry coverage, Prisma use, and test gaps.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to add a user endpoint.
output: A route delegates request handling to a controller.
The controller validates input and calls a service.
The service owns business rules and uses a repository.
Tests cover success, validation failure, and authorization behavior.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a route file contains too much logic.
output: The response identifies business rules inside the route.
It recommends moving logic to a service.
It keeps request parsing and response formatting in the controller.

output_examples.input: A team wants consistent error tracking.
output: The response recommends centralized error handling.
It adds Sentry capture at boundaries.
It calls out sensitive data that should be filtered before reporting.

best_practices: Use the skill when changing routes, controllers, services, repositories, middleware, validation, monitoring, or tests.
Review generated examples against project security, privacy, and deployment rules before production use.
Keep business logic in services and database access in repositories.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder secrets or development credentials into production configuration.
Do not place long business workflows directly inside route handlers.
Do not enable broad telemetry fields without checking privacy requirements.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, and Sentry based backend services.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill with patterns and examples for backend development.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes validation, error handling, secrets guidance, and testing practices, but production security still needs review.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing services?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes migration and refactoring guidance for moving legacy routes toward layered architecture.

faq.question: What should users verify before applying examples?
faq.answer: Users should verify secrets handling, telemetry fields, authorization rules, database access, and project-specific compliance needs.
